source.title: Adaptive and interpretable two-sample test as a batch-level tool for AI safety
source.authors: Gaia Grosso; Arnau Marin-Llobet; Demba E. Ba

record.tranche_reason: The study discusses and geometrically compares with the refusal direction, but its own results concern attack-prompt activation geometry and batch detection, not whether the direction causes refusal or the other listed claim versions hold.
record.gate_note: The paper reproduces the refusal direction for a geometric comparison and reports its cosine similarities to attack-probe directions; these are recorded below. Its NP detection-power results, attack-campaign detection rates, and probe TPR results concern detection rather than the refusal behavior or mechanism in the claim. The authors explicitly distinguish their input-representation geometry from causal mediation of refusal.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces the Arditi et al. refusal direction for Llama-3-8B-Instruct only to compare its cosine similarity with attack-prompt probe directions at layer 16. It does not ablate or add the direction, and it reports no refusal rates. Its own results concern detection power and the geometry of attack-prompt inputs. The authors state in A.4 that this 'says nothing about whether a single direction suffices to mediate refusal.' So none of V1–V8 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right, but it hides an inconsistency. Appendix A.4 says the refusal-direction comparison says nothing about whether one direction mediates refusal. The abstract and conclusion go further: they say the geometry 'contradicts a single-refusal-direction account' and is 'richer than a single refusal direction can capture.' The paraphrase should note that the headline claim overstates what the authors' own caveat allows; the evidence is input-representation geometry only.
record.recipe_differences: The main method is adaptive Neyman–Pearson two-sample testing with sparse kernels on activation batches. The authors reproduce the refusal direction only for a cosine-geometry comparison; they do not apply the original refusal ablation/addition intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama-3-8B-Instruct at layer 16, the reproduced refusal direction has cosine 0.34 with the direct-harmful probe and 0.10–0.17 with the other attack probes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction acts like a supervised probe on direct harmful inputs. It aligns weakly with the input representations of scaffolded and optimized jailbreak prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Attack-prompt features in Llama-3-8B-Instruct form two near-orthogonal clusters, scaffolded and direct. Benign WildChat prompts populate both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak-prompt activations split along a structural axis of conversational framing, not a single attack direction.

fits_no_version.finding: In Granite Guardian 3.1-8B, attack-campaign signals form a single cluster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harm-classifier fine-tuning can collapse the scaffolded/direct structure in attack-prompt representations.

record.peer_reviewed: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, 2026
record.problems: The refusal-direction comparison is representational and has no refusal-behavior intervention; the authors themselves state that it does not establish whether one direction mediates refusal. No general-capability preservation test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Batch-level detector power, live campaign detection rates, two-sample baselines, and supervised-probe TPR results were left out because they measure detection performance rather than refusal-direction behavior or causal mediation.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction, no refusal-rate measurement, and no capability check.

No test of whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction, and no adversarial training against its ablation. The low cosines between attack probes and the refusal direction concern input geometry, not suppression.
The multi-subspace geometry describes attack-prompt inputs, not the refusal mechanism. No affine, cone or multi-direction refusal intervention is tested.
Harm judgment and refusal are not measured separately. The Granite Guardian geometry is a classifier's harm representation with no refusal decision.
No transfer across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly unlinked. The cosine comparison is at layer 16, while Arditi's selected layer is about 12, which the authors say makes a comparison there ill-posed. No row should be read as evidence for or against V1 or V4. A researcher might misread the abstract's 'single refusal direction' language as a V4 challenge; it is not one, because there is no causal or behavioural test.

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition of the direction is evaluated for refusal behavior, and no effect on general capability is tested.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration evaluation.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

The study reports multiple subspaces for attack-prompt activations, but does not test whether refusal itself is represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions. The authors state that their representational results do not establish whether one direction mediates refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or training stages for whether a removable direction forms.

rows.subject: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Reproduced the refusal direction using the cited paper's public pipeline and measured cosine similarity to the direct-harmful probe direction.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between refusal direction and attack-probe direction
rows.note: This is a representational alignment measurement, not a test of refusal behavior or causal mediation.

rows.subject: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Reproduced the refusal direction using the cited paper's public pipeline and measured cosine similarities to the other attack subspaces.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between refusal direction and attack-probe directions
rows.note: The reported range is for the other attack subspaces collectively. The authors interpret this as weak alignment, not as evidence about whether one direction mediates refusal.

rows.subject: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Clustered features discovered in jailbreak-prompt activations and compared their geometry.
rows.value: Features form two near-orthogonal macro-clusters: scaffolded prompts and direct prompts.
rows.note: The study reports attack-prompt representation geometry. It does not establish that refusal itself requires more than one direction.

rows.subject: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Projected benign WildChat prompts into the discovered feature geometry and assessed which attack-prompt clusters they occupied.
rows.measure: Occupancy of scaffolded and direct activation clusters
rows.value: WildChat prompts populate both clusters, including a substantial fraction in the scaffolded cluster.
rows.note: The authors interpret the clusters as reflecting conversational structure in general, rather than a safety-specific feature.

rows.subject: Granite Guardian 3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Clustered features discovered in attack-campaign activations.

conditions.value: PAIR, TAP, Best-of-N, and Crescendo campaigns

rows.value: Attack signals collapse into a single cluster.
rows.note: This is the guard's attack-signal geometry, not a measurement of refusal-direction mediation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
